query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a controlled minor amount of Sn to equiatomic FeCoNi will induce the formation of nanoscale BCC regions within the dominant fcc matrix, thereby enhancing domain wall pinning and increasing the coercivity compared to the pure fcc alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic FeCoNi high-entropy alloy that crystallizes as a single-phase face‐centered cubic (fcc) solid solution with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field.
generation.intervention: Introduce a small, optimized amount of Sn as a compositional addition while keeping the overall alloy near equiatomic proportions.
generation.conditions: Process the alloy via high-temperature annealing (or rapid thermal annealing) under conditions that favor the nucleation of a secondary BCC phase while maintaining a high configurational entropy (≥1.0R).
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of fine BCC precipitates embedded in the fcc matrix which act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
generation.mechanism: The Sn addition perturbs the phase stability such that a partial transformation from the majority fcc structure to a minor BCC phase occurs. The BCC phase, having a lower symmetry and higher intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy, enhances domain wall pinning. This increased pinning leads to a higher coercivity, although there may be a moderate change in saturation magnetization.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline pure fcc FeCoNi alloy, the Sn-doped alloy is expected to exhibit a notably higher coercive field due to enhanced domain wall pinning from the BCC precipitates, while still maintaining acceptable saturation magnetization.
generation.baseline: The equiatomic FeCoNi alloy in its unmodified single-phase fcc state.
generation.boundary: The effectiveness of the intervention depends on carefully optimizing the Sn content; too little may not trigger sufficient BCC phase formation, while too much could reduce overall entropy or lead to excessive phase separation that degrades other magnetic properties.
generation.uncertainty: The precise Sn concentration required and the magnitude of the coercivity increase are not fully determined and may vary with processing conditions. There is also a trade-off risk with potential reductions in saturation magnetization.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples under identical processing conditions: (a) the baseline equiatomic FeCoNi alloy and (b) a series of FeCoNi alloys with incrementally added Sn (e.g., at varied minor atomic percentages). Use high-temperature annealing to promote phase formation. Conduct phase analysis by X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy to verify the presence and scale of any BCC precipitates. Measure magnetic hysteresis loops using a vibrating sample magnetometer to extract coercivity and saturation magnetization values.
measurements: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images for phase identification
Magnetic hysteresis loops (VSM) to determine coercivity and saturation magnetization
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Sn-doped samples do not show a statistically significant increase (e.g., greater than 20% relative improvement) in coercivity compared to the baseline FeCoNi alloy, or if the induced phase separation negatively impacts the overall magnetic properties such that performance criteria are not met, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: In summary, we have achieved high magnetic anisotropy in rare‐earth‐free high entropy metallic thin films by sputtering and RTA. Robust magnetic order of both fcc FeCoNiMnCu and L10 (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt films has been demonstrated. The FeCoNiMnCu films exhibit a large coercivity increase after RTA, resulting from microstructural changes and strain‐induced anisotropy enhancement which strengthens domain wall pinning. Addition of Pt reduces the symmetry of the cubic fcc lattice to an intermetallic tetragonal L10 phase of (FeCoNiMnCu)Pt. Although the Pt insertion lowers the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, the entropy is still high enough to stabilize an L10 single phase. This intermetallic phase is confirmed to host high magnetocrystalline anisotropy, likely attributed to the lower symmetry of the L10 structure and the strong spin‐orbit coupling provided by the Pt insertion. These findings demonstrate the promise of high‐entropy intermetallic design as a key avenue to search for new high‐entropy magnets beyond the equiatomic composition.

The present work exhibits the effects of Sn addition on the magnetic properties and microstructure of FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) high-entropy alloys (HEAs). The results show all the samples consist of a mixed structure of face-centered-cubic (FCC) phase and body-centered-cubic (BCC) phase. The addition of Sn promotes the formation of BCC phase, and it also affects the shape of Cu-rich nano-precipitates in BCC matrix. It also shows that the Curie temperatures (Tc) of the FCC phase and the saturation magnetization (Ms) of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs increase greatly while the remanence (Br) decreases after the addition of Sn into FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8 HEA. The thermomagnetic curves indicate that the phases of the FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs will transform from FCC with low Tc to BCC phase with high Tc at temperature of 600–700 K. This work provides a new idea for FeCoNi(CuAl)0.8Snx (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.10) HEAs for their potential application as soft magnets to be used at high temperatures.
